facts.text: Tanglin’s name comes from the Teochew “Twa Tang Leng,” meaning “great east hill peaks,” reflecting the surrounding hills.
The Singapore Botanic Gardens, a UNESCO World Heritage Site founded in 1859, lies within Tanglin and is the city’s oldest garden.
Dempsey Hill, once a British military barracks, now hosts upscale restaurants and galleries, illustrating Tanglin’s military‑to‑lifestyle conversion.
Tanglin hosts the headquarters of Singapore’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Interpol’s regional office, giving the area a diplomatic gravitas.
The Museum of Ice Cream opened in 2021 on Loewen Road, adding a quirky cultural spot to Tanglin’s lineup.
Tanglin’s main transport links include Farrer Road, Botanic Gardens, and Stevens MRT stations, connecting it to the Circle, Downtown, and Thomson‑East Coast lines.
